newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end limit up on Japan tariff cut prospect.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end limit up on Japan tariff cut prospect.

text.p: Word that Japan's pork tariff may be cut early due to rising pork prices there boosted CME hog futures to sharply higher to limit closes after many months set new contract highs, traders said.

Hogs closed up the 2.000-cent-a-lb limit to 0.775 cents higher with April and June limit up at the closing bell. April April settled at 73.975 cents. July through next year July contracts posted new contract highs. July ended at 82.125 cents a lb, just off its new high of 82.325 cents.
Pork bellies slipped from best levels to end 1.875 to 0.600 higher with May up most at 80.175 cents per lb. February posted a new contract high 72.950 cents

"Are we going to see those (Japanese) tariffs relaxed or what, has got the whole industry by hostage over there and that's the story that's keeping us firm," said Don Roose, president U.S. Commodities Inc.

Japan initially said it would keep its tariff on pork imports until July 1 despite Taiwan's pork export ban. That news for a time, weighed on nearby CME hog futures despite ideas of eventual increased exports.
